title: Protocol for Extraction and Electron Microscopy Visualization of Lipids in Viburnum tinus Fruit Using Cryo-Ultramicrotomy
protocol: Pour liquid nitrogen into a stainless steel Dewar.
Place the lower half of a small container in the liquid nitrogen to cool down to its temperature.
Fill the cooled container with ethane gas until it liquidizes.
Peel pericarp of fresh V. tinus fruit with a razor blade.
Blot excess juice with a piece of filter paper.
Cut the peeled epicarp into a strip with dimensions of approximately 3 mm (L) × 1 mm (W).
Cut a strip of filter paper with dimensions of approximately 5 mm (L) × 3 mm (W).
Spread carbon adhesive paste on half of the filter paper strip.
Place the epicarp on the edge of the filter paper strip so that only its lower half is in contact with the carbon paste.
Let the carbon paste dry to ensure the pericarp adheres well to the filter paper strip.
Hold the filter paper part of the specimen with tweezers.
Quench the specimen in liquid ethane and let it freeze for about 10 seconds.
Transfer the frozen specimen to liquid nitrogen in a polystyrene container.
Transfer the frozen specimen from the polystyrene container to the cryochamber using tweezers precooled in liquid nitrogen.
Fix the filter paper part of the specimen in the flat clamp of the specimen holder and let the specimen temperature equilibrate to −110°C.
Rotate the knife holder to put the trimming tool in the cutting position and approach the trimming tool to the tip of the specimen.
Trim the specimen using the trimming tool to make a surface with dimensions of approximately 0.1 mm (L) × 0.05 mm (W).
Rotate the knife holder to set the diamond knife in the cutting position and approach the knife to the specimen surface.
Hold the glow-discharged grid with tweezers and insert the tweezers into a micromanipulator of the cryochamber.
Using the micrometer gauges of the micromanipulator, place the grid slightly below the diamond knife.
Activate the discharge function of the antistatic device.
Cut ultrathin sections of thickness about 90 nm.
Transfer the sections to the grid surface using an eyelash.
Disactivate the discharge function of the antistatic device.
Retract the grid from the knife using micrometer gauges.
Remove the grid from the cryochamber and let it warm up to room temperature under nitrogen gas or dry air flow.
Mount the grid in a standard TEM holder.
Insert the holder into the TEM for observation.
Adjust the sample position to the eucentric height.
Perform TEM alignment if necessary.
Set up Low Dose mode in SerialEM at a blank (non-specimen) area.
Ensure that the overall radiation dose does not exceed 4 e-/Å−1.
Set the magnification to ×6,000–10,000 for Record and Focus areas.
Set the magnification to ×2,000–4,000 for View area.
Set the target defocus value at −5–10 μm.
Acquire images of the sections using the Low Dose mode.
Ensure the specimen is an unfixed and unstained biological tissue to minimize radiation damage.
Take a low magnification image of the sections at ×100–600.
Remove the grid from the TEM.
Put the grid on a filter paper strip.
Place the strip on the sample holder of the reflux extractor.
Insert the holder into the extractor and tilt it by about 20°.
Treat the grid with refluxed chloroform for 10–20 minutes.
Ensure that condensed chloroform flows down from the sample holder.
Remove the grid from the extractor and let it dry in air.
Insert the treated grid back into the TEM.
Observe the previously observed area of the specimen under the same low dose condition.
Compare the image contrast of the same view field before and after chloroform extraction.
